This PR also fixes #18351 ("readJson() lacks error handling for malformed JSON"), which is currently open with no associated PR.

The change to `packages/core/src/filesystem.ts` — wrapping `JSON.parse` in `Effect.try` and surfacing a typed `FileSystemError` instead of letting the parse throw as an uncatchable Effect defect — is exactly what #18351 asks for, and it satisfies its acceptance criteria (meaningful error tied to the file/method, original cause preserved).

It also resolves a separate crash path: `opencode mcp list` / `mcp auth` dies with `JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token u0000` when `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json` is corrupt. `McpAuth.all()` already guards with `.pipe(Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed({})))`, but because the old `readJson` threw the parse error as a defect (not the typed error channel), `Effect.catch` never caught it. With this fix the fallback works and the command degrades gracefully. (Tracked in #18351; symptom also reported in #25008.)

Consider adding `Closes #18351` to the description.

Rebased onto current `dev` (post-#29068) — now mergeable, CI green.

Both issues this closes are still live on `dev`:

- **#26929** — `OutputFormatText`/`OutputFormatJsonSchema` in `packages/core/src/session/legacy.ts` are still `Schema.Class`, so encoding a plain DB row crashes `GET /session/:id/message`. Converted both to `Schema.Struct`, matching the rest of the file.
- **#25430** — `prompt.ts` still constructs `StructuredOutputError` with a hardcoded `retries: 0`. This wires `format.retryCount` (default 2): on a structured-output miss, runLoop persists a synthetic `<system-reminder>` user message carrying the prior format forward and re-runs the step with `toolChoice: "required"` still in force, then reports the real count when it finally gives up.

It complements the existing `STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` — the prompt nudges the model to call the tool up front; this recovers when the nudge doesn't take.

@thdxr — tagging you since this lands on the `legacy` path you just moved in #29068. Happy to retarget at the new `SessionMessage` surface instead if that's where structured output is headed.

some AI-assisted notes (that make sense to my human brain):

I think this is the remaining half of the OpenTUI `ScrollBoxRenderable` `_hasManualScroll` lifecycle issue, rather than opencode session rendering itself.

opencode’s TUI session view uses OpenTUI sticky scroll:

```tsx
<scrollbox stickyScroll={true} stickyStart="bottom" ...>
```

The related OpenTUI fix in anomalyco/opentui#1088 has already merged and appears to be in the @opentui/core version used by opencode 1.15.13. That fix addressed the opposite symptom: sticky scroll fighting the user while they are reading history during streaming.

This issue looks like the inverse/re-engagement failure:

1. User scrolls up during streaming.
2. OpenTUI marks `_hasManualScroll = true`, correctly pausing sticky-bottom behavior.
3. User scrolls back to the bottom.
4. `scrollTop` / `updateStickyState()` can detect the sticky edge and clear `_hasManualScroll`.
5. But the outer mouse/key scroll handlers still unconditionally set `_hasManualScroll = true` after handling scroll input.
6. That can override the “back at bottom” reset.
7. On the next content resize, `recalculateBarProps()` sees `_hasManualScroll === true`, so it does not reapply `stickyStart="bottom"`.
8. New content is appended below the viewport and auto-scroll appears stuck off.
9. 
This matches the still-open OpenTUI PR anomalyco/opentui#816:
https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/pull/816

That PR specifically calls out:

> `onMouseEvent` and `handleKeyPress` both unconditionally set `_hasManualScroll = true` after scroll events, overriding the correct state set by the scrollTop/scrollLeft setters and updateStickyState(). This caused `_hasManualScroll` to be permanently stuck on true after any scroll event — even when the user scrolled back to the bottom.

So my guess is: opencode 1.15.13 has the merged #1088 fix, but not the remaining #816 re-engagement fix.

## Detailed model information

### grok-composer-2.5-fast

Grok Build's composer model for agentic code composition.

**API probe results (June 2, 2026):**

| Feature | Status |
|---------|--------|
| `/v1/chat/completions` | ✅ HTTP 200 |
| `tool_use` (function calling) | ✅ Returns `tool_calls` with forced `tool_choice` |
| `reasoning_content` field | ✅ Returned in response |
| System prompt | ✅ |
| Multi-turn | ✅ |
| Temperature control | ✅ |
| `stop` sequences | ❌ 400 (unsupported) |
| `/v1/models` listing | ❌ Hidden model |

**Pricing** (from `cost_in_usd_ticks`): ~$1.00/M input, ~$2.00/M output

### grok-4.3

xAI's flagship model. $1.25/M input, $2.50/M output, 1M context window. Already available via the xAI API but was missing from the Zen table.

### grok-4.20-0309-reasoning

Deep reasoning model with extended thinking. $1.25/M input, $2.50/M output. Supports `reasoningEffort` — but `transform.ts` already handles Grok reasoning variants correctly, so no code change needed.

### No runtime code changes

`transform.ts` line 671: `if (id.includes("grok")) return {}` catches all Grok models that don't match the `grok-3-mini` specific reasoning path. This PR only adds docs.

### Adoption context

Already adopted by [progrok](https://github.com/lidge-jun/progrok), [ima2-gen](https://github.com/lidge-jun/ima2-gen), [hermes-agent PR #36968](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/36968), and [openclaw PR #89190](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89190).

Opencode has built-in equivalents for all the standard filesystem MCP tools (filesystem_read_file, filesystem_write_file, filesystem_edit_file, filesystem_create_directory, filesystem_list_directory, filesystem_search_files, filesystem_get_file_info, etc.) — and they respect the permission system (plan mode's edit: deny, read rules, etc.).
